content.text:
I read the structure in four regions, left to right.

**Left end (thalidomide-type unit):** a glutarimide ring, O=C1CCC(N2...)C(=O)N1, is attached through its 3-position to the isoindoline-1,3-dione nitrogen. The 4-position of the isoindoline carries an NH.

**Linker:** from that NH the chain runs NH-CH2CH2-O-CH2CH2-O-CH2CH2-O-CH2CH2-O-CH2CH2-O-CH2CH2-C(=O). I counted the oxygens along the chain in the drawing: 5 (at x = 575, 733, 888, 1045 and 1205). The chain from the NH starts with CH2CH2 to the first O, then CH2CH2 to the second O, and so on, ending with O-CH2CH2-C(=O). That gives 4 ethylene units between NH and the fifth O (to O1, O2, O3, O4), then a fifth ethylene to O5. Checking against the drawing: the bonds from NH go to the first O, then a zigzag to the next O, and so on, so each O-to-O gap is two carbons. The five oxygens therefore need five CH2CH2 units before them, and then CH2CH2C(=O) follows the last O.

**Amide and phenylene:** the C(=O) is bonded to NH, which is bonded to a para-substituted benzene. The other para position carries an NH.

**Right end:** that NH is bonded to C2 of the pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidine. C4 of the pyrimidine carries a pyrazol-4-yl group, and the pyrazole N1 bears a propyl chain. The pyrrole nitrogen is NH.

Assembled SMILES:

O=C1CCC(N2C(=O)c3c(NCCOCCOCCOCCOCCOCCC(=O)Nc4ccc(Nc5nc(-c6cnn(CCC)c6)c6cc[nH]c6n5)cc4)cccc3C2=O)C(=O)N1

I did not check the propyl chain against the drawing beyond its three drawn carbons.
